newsitem.title: TURKEY: Kurd group says takes mountain from foe in Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Kurd group says takes mountain from foe in Iraq.

text.p: An Iraqi Kurdish faction said on Monday it had gained control of a strategic mountain in northern Iraq from another militia but denied a report by its rival of clashes that could endanger Western-brokered peace efforts.
"There was no fighting because the PUK forces fled from the area," Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) spokesman Faik Nerweyi told Reuters.
The Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) said earlier that two of its militiamen had died at the weekend in fighting over the Didevan mountain.
"KDP forces attacked on November 30 at Didevan, a mountain 30-km (18-miles) southwest of Koy Sanjak town and they took it from us," PUK Ankara representative Shazad Saib told Reuters.
"The clashes continued yesterday, killing two PUK fighters," he said.

The two sides have held several rounds of peace talks under U.S., British and Turkish mediation since they declared a ceasefire in October to end months of fighting that increased Baghdad's influence in the mountainous region.
"It is a very negative indication for the future of the peace talks," Saib said.
Iraqi troops and tanks helped Massoud Barzani's KDP take the key city of Arbil from the rival faction in August, prompting U.S. missile strikes on Iraqi targets in retaliation.

The Kurds broke from Baghdad after the 1991 Gulf War under the shield of U.S.-led allied air patrols over the region. Turkey and Washington are discussing the future of the flights, due to be reviewed by the end of the year, Turkish officials said.
Numerous ceasefires between the Kurds have been announced and broken since fighting first flared up in 1994. Neighbouring Turkey said it hoped the latest tension was isolated.

"We heard those reports over the weekend but we are hoping that those clashes are local in nature and will not effect their ongoing efforts to strenghten the ceasefire," foreign ministry spokesman Sermet Atacanli told a news briefing.
The two factions have been unable to agree on the distribution of toll money from the KDP-held Habur crossing into Turkey and the status of Arbil.
